newsitem.title: USA: Florida international trade up 11.5 pct in 1997 Q1.
newsitem.headline: Florida international trade up 11.5 pct in 1997 Q1.

text.p: The value of merchandise shipped internationally through Florida ports totalled $14.5 billion in the first quarter of 1997, an increase of 11.5 percent over the same period last year, according to a report released Tuesday.
Fertilizer, mainly from Florida's phosphate mining operations, was the top export for the January-through-March period.
Passenger vehicles were the top import, according to the report by Enterprise Florida, the public-private partnership that assumed some duties of the state's former commerce department.
Brazil was Florida's top trading partner, accounting for $1.66 billion of goods. Japan was next, followed by Venezuela, the Dominican Republic and Colombia.
